pages.text: "Wow, a green pebble!" Riri in her yellow hat picked up a smooth stone on the beach. In the summer sun, it shone sea-green. Lolo in yellow boots ran over and grabbed it.
"I saw it first! It is going in my pocket!" Riri pulled. "No, I held it first!" Lolo pulled too. This way, that way—both faces turned red.
Their hands slipped, and the pebble flew away. Both fell with a thump, throwing up sand. The green stone hid in the wet sand.
They dug, but the green stone was nowhere. "Your fault!" "You pushed!" They sat with their backs turned. Only the waves splashed in and out.
Dad the fisherman knelt between them. "Pulling sends stones flying and hurts feelings. What about words instead of shoves?" His hand swept the wet sand, uncovering the green stone.
Dad set it on the sand between them. "Now try words." Riri spoke first. "Lolo, I really wanted this stone." Lolo placed a hand beside it too. "So did I. What shall we do?"
"Riri's pocket today, Lolo's tomorrow!" Lolo clapped both hands. Riri slipped the green stone into her pocket. "Use words, not shoves!"
They sat side by side, looking for more shiny stones. Riri counted what she found. Lolo splashed boots into the edge of the water and offered another stone.

Now they knew how not to fight. One, let go of the hands that are pulling! Two, say you want it! Three, me today, you tomorrow! Even finding one spiral shell together that evening, they did not quarrel.
Dad held one hand from each and walked home. Pulling sends the stone away, but words let both have it. Riri placed the green stone in Lolo's hand. "Tomorrow is your turn. Use words, not shoves!"
